subject: koch

brief.inclusion: Koch chairman and Stand Together founder who spent decades building a durable network linking private business wealth to scholarship, advocacy, litigation and elections.

summary: Charles Koch has led the family company now called Koch, Inc. since 1967 and remains its chairman and co-chief executive. With his late brother David and a succession of institutional partners, he built a libertarian-influenced network spanning universities, think tanks, litigation, community programs and electoral groups—now organized chiefly through Stand Together and Americans for Prosperity.

statements.summary: Koch said he regretted the degree to which his network's work had become identified with partisan division.
Koch argued that durable change comes from enabling people closest to problems rather than imposing top-down solutions.
He defined good profit as the result of creating value for customers and society rather than seeking privilege.
Koch describes Principle Based Management as a framework for long-term value creation and meaningful contribution.
His network states that every person should have the opportunity to realize their potential.

chapters.title: Engineer and heir
chapters.body:
Charles Koch was born in Wichita in 1935, one of Fred Koch's sons. He earned three engineering degrees from MIT before returning to the family enterprise [[koch-bio, britannica-koch]].

The inheritance gave him a company; it did not predetermine its later scale. His public philosophy fused engineering, Austrian economics and organizational incentives [[koch-book-2015]].

chapters.title: Transforming Koch
chapters.dek: A regional business becomes a private conglomerate
chapters.body:
Koch became chairman and CEO in 1967. The company expanded from oil gathering into refining, chemicals, manufacturing, consumer products, technology and investment [[koch-bio]].

In 2023 he became co-CEO while remaining chairman. Because Koch is private, Forbes's wealth estimate depends largely on modeled family ownership rather than a public market price [[koch-leadership, forbes-koch-2026]].

chapters.title: A management philosophy
chapters.body:
Koch developed Market-Based Management, now called Principle Based Management, to translate property rights, incentives and dispersed knowledge into company practice [[koch-book-2015, koch-bio]].

His books present profit as legitimate when earned by creating value, while critics argue that Koch companies also benefited from regulatory and political power. The profile distinguishes his stated theory from outcomes attributed by critics [[koch-book-2015, jane-mayer-2016]].

chapters.title: Building an intellectual infrastructure
chapters.body:
Koch helped build IHS, Cato and Mercatus, financing scholarship, fellowships and policy research over decades [[cato-history, koch-bio, cssn-koch-2024]].

Support does not make every scholar a Koch agent. The institutional strategy matters because it creates personnel and arguments that persist beyond any candidate or election [[jane-mayer-2016]].

chapters.title: From seminars to Stand Together
chapters.body:
Beginning in 2003, Koch convened donors around shared investments in policy and civil society. Americans for Prosperity became the best-known grassroots arm [[afp-about, jane-mayer-2016]].

The network adopted the Stand Together name in 2019 and broadened its public emphasis to education, poverty, criminal justice and community problem-solving. Brian Hooks runs the network; Charles Koch remains its founder and central patron [[politico-rebrand-2019, stand-together-about]].

chapters.title: Selective Republican power
chapters.dek: A network larger than a personal contribution ledger
chapters.body:
Koch-aligned groups helped elect Republicans and oppose Obama-era policy, but the network withheld presidential support from Trump in 2016 and 2020 [[newyorker-koch-2010, time-afp-2024]].

AFP Action endorsed Nikki Haley in 2023, then stopped presidential spending as Trump consolidated the nomination. The episode shows both the network's scale and the limits of donor influence over voters [[time-afp-2024]].

chapters.title: Beyond partisan alignment
chapters.dek: Criminal justice and a public course correction
chapters.body:
Koch organizations worked with left-leaning partners on criminal-justice reform, including the First Step Act. These coalitions reflected libertarian limits on state coercion as well as a strategic broadening [[wp-koch-network-2018, koch-book-2020]].

In 2020 Koch said excessive partisanship had been a mistake. The shift changed rhetoric and some partnerships, but Stand Together remained a major force in Republican electoral politics [[nyt-koch-trump-2020, time-afp-2024]].

chapters.title: Present influence
chapters.dek: A mature network with multiple channels
chapters.body:
At ninety, Koch remains chairman and co-CEO of the company and founder of a network that claims nearly $8 billion in lifetime nonprofit giving [[koch-bio, stand-together-about]].

His personal FEC total is a poor proxy for influence. Grants, advocacy, litigation, scholarship and AFP Action spending operate through organizations, while the network's 2026 civic campaign shows continued investment outside elections [[fec-koch, ap-stand-together-2026]].
